newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rise, sustained by local funds.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rise, sustained by local funds.

text.p: Argentine stocks finished higher Monday, sustained by local fund buying.
Still, traders reported some caution ahead of Tuesday's presidential election in the United States.
The blue chip Merval index rose 1.45 percent to 582.26 index points.
The buying was backed by higher trading activity, with $15.3 million worth of shares changing hands compared with 10.5 million on Friday.
Traders said stocks' gains were also helped by firmer bonds in the local market.
"Technically nothing has changed; the main trend is higher and as long as economic indicators show improvements, the market is likely to rise," said an investor note by Banco Credito Argentino.
Traders added that the market was behaving with a great amount of selectivity, as it kept an eye on the imminent release of quarterly results by companies.
Market players said they also expected some caution in coming days because of the U.S. election, which could have an impact on U.S. stock markets and bonds.

"One should be cautious and keep a close eye on the Dow Jones. Investors are not putting a lot of money into the market until they see the result of the U.S. election," said Gabriel Armando, an analyst at Galicia Valores.
Some 68 shares were traded this session, of which 33 rose, six declined and the rest were stable.

Among the largest stocks traded on the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange, textile company Alpargatas and food company Molinos posted the largest gains, with increases of 4.5 percent and 4.0 percent respectively.
